summary: Secure LAN discovery, single-parent adoption, and full mTLS hardening (pairing protocol) between the myseliasan control plane and mymatasan nodes. A new shared infra/pairing package implements authenticated UDP multicast discovery (HMAC-SHA256 signed probes and announces with nonce + timestamp replay protection) and exported helpers for the HTTPS adoption assertion. On the node side (mymatasan): a new IPairingService persists all state in the existing RuntimeSetting KV store (pairing.state, pairing.fleetKey and pairing.enrollment encrypted at rest via infra/atrest, pairing.nodeId); public HTTP routes POST /api/pairing/adopt (fleet-key assertion + single-use claim code) and POST /api/pairing/release (pairing token) are callable without a session by the control plane; protected routes (GET /api/pairing/status, POST /api/pairing/claim-code, POST /api/pairing/unpair, PUT /api/pairing/fleet-key) are behind local-session + admin middleware. The discovery responder (infra/pairing.Responder) answers probes only when unpaired and a fleet key is set; it goes silent immediately after adoption. A new EnrollmentManager (services/node_enrollment.go) runs after adoption: it generates an ECDSA P-256 key + CSR locally (private key never leaves the node), POSTs the CSR to the control plane's POST /api/nodes/enroll (authenticated by the pairing token), stores the issued cert bundle (AES-256-GCM encrypted), and serves a mutual-TLS management listener on pairing.mtlsPort (default 49532) with GET /heartbeat and POST /release; it renews the cert before pairing.renewBeforeHours (default 48h) of expiry and reconciles on a 5-minute timer or an immediate Kick triggered by the adopt callback. On the control-plane side (myseliasan): a new INodeRegistry service manages fleet-key CRUD, LAN scan, Adopt (builds signed assertion, POSTs to node, stores ManagedNode with MTLSPort), a new Enroll method (token-authenticated CSR signing via the on-prem fleet CA), Release (revokes cert, prefers mTLS release, drops row), Heartbeat (mTLS probe of all adopted nodes on configurable interval), and MarkSelfDropped. The on-prem fleet CA (infra/fleetca + apps/myseliasan/services/fleet_ca.go) is a self-contained ECDSA P-256 CA with a 10-year root persisted in ControlSetting; it mints 7-day (default, configurable) node certs and a 90-day control-plane client cert; revocation is a denylist (refuse-to-renew + short TTL, no CRL/OCSP). HTTP routes under /api/nodes expose all registry operations to authenticated operators; a public POST /api/nodes/enroll is the node-initiated cert-signing endpoint; a public POST /api/nodes/self-dropped accepts fleet-key-signed self-drop notices. A new Mymatasan view in the myseliasan SPA provides fleet-key management, LAN scan, adopt form, and an adopted-nodes table with Release. PairingConfigModel gained four new fields (pairing.mtlsPort, pairing.certTtlHours, pairing.renewBeforeHours, pairing.heartbeatIntervalSeconds) wired in both apps. The mymatasan first-run setup wizard gained an optional Connectivity step to configure the fleet key and claim code. The myseliasan frontend was rebuilt from a hand-written vanilla page into a React/webpack SPA (apps/myseliasan/views/react-webpack) mirroring mymatasan's architecture, reusing mymatasan's app.css + icons.js and a separate controlplane.css; its api() helper sends the federated double-submit CSRF token (X-CSRF-Token from the __Host-kopiv2_csrf/kopiv2_csrf cookie) on state-changing requests, without which node actions returned 403. Discovery was made multi-homed-reliable: the responder (binds 0.0.0.0:port) and prober now join/send the multicast group on every multicast-capable interface via golang.org/x/net/ipv4 with multicast loopback, fixing 'scan finds nothing' on hosts with Hyper-V/WSL/VPN adapters and on same-host dev (cross-platform Linux/macOS/Windows). UX: copy-to-clipboard buttons for the fleet key (myseliasan) and claim code (mymatasan), and the mymatasan Connectivity panel polls pairing status every 4s so control-plane adoption/release updates its panels in place without a manual refresh.
compatibility: Backward compatible. The pairing subsystem is disabled at the protocol level (node is undiscoverable) until an operator explicitly sets a fleet key on both sides; no existing behavior changes. pairing.enabled defaults to true but has no effect until a fleet key is configured. The new pairing.mtlsPort (default 49532), pairing.certTtlHours (default 168 / 7 days), pairing.renewBeforeHours (default 48), and pairing.heartbeatIntervalSeconds (default 60) config keys have safe defaults and do not need to be added to existing config files. The RuntimeSetting and ControlSetting rows written by the pairing/enrollment services are additive; existing databases are unaffected. The ManagedNode.MTLSPort and ManagedNode.CertExpiresAt columns are new; the bootstrap auto-migration adds them. The ManagedNode.Fingerprint column remains present but is unused (identity verification uses the cert CN, not a pinned fingerprint). Nodes adopted before this change will not have a cert; they will obtain one automatically on next restart once the EnrollmentManager runs its first reconcile cycle. golang.org/x/net is promoted from an indirect to a direct dependency. Operational note (not a code change): the host firewall must allow inbound UDP on the discovery port (49531) and TCP on the mTLS port (49532), and Docker's default bridge does not forward multicast (use host networking or manual IP+port adoption).
